catalog_citation: Sneddon, J.N. 1975. Tondano Phonology and Grammar. Pacific Linguistics B-38. Canberra: ANU. (sealang.net/CRCL online edition)
catalog_quote: Word stress is treated as phonemic because its placement does not appear to be always predictable on purely phonological grounds. ... No instances of minimal stress contrast have been recorded but contrast in terms of CVCV structure does occur. ... Stress usually falls on the penultimate syllable of the word: /wale/ [wálɛ] house ... Word stress shifts from the penultimate syllable under the following conditions: (a) A long vocoid, which is interpreted as two phonemic syllable nuclei, takes stress if it is in the last or second-last phonetic syllable in the word: /kinaaŋku/ [kiná:ŋku] ... /tikoo/ [tikó:] throat. If both the last and second-last phonetic syllables contain long vocoids, then the last takes stress ... (b) If the penultimate syllable nucleus is /ə/ the following changes occur: (i) Stress falls on the final syllable if its nucleus is a vowel other than /ə/ and it is separated…

Sneddon /təmpok/ [tə́mpɔk]) and add a caution that Brickell's own data contain closed-final words with penult stress (patoto'an, pesesiwon, wangko) and that he and Sneddon disagree on /rəpət/ (Sneddon [rə́pət], Brickell [rɘ.pɘ́t]); add Brickell 2014 to refs.

sources.quote: 'In Tondano stress is non-contrastive. Although there is some unpredictability in stress placement, there are certain environments that will always affect stress assignment. These are: Vowel length; Syllable structure and syllable weight, specifically whether syllables are open or closed; Occurrence of schwa as nucleus in a penultimate syllable.' (p. 57). 'Stress placement on the penultimate syllable appears to be the default stress assignment' (asu [á.su], lansuna [lan.sú.na], saribata [sa.ri.bá.ta]; enclitics =mow/=ku 'are not counted for stress') (pp. 57-58). sources.note: Newest full fieldwork grammar (Glottolog's top-ranked grammar, 498 pp); its section 2.5 adds closed-syllable weight (final CVC attracting stress: oki' [o.kíʔ], lodèy [lo.dɛ́j]) to Sneddon's long-vowel and schwa conditions, which bears on our weight class (currently CVV only). downloaded now.

sources.quote: OT reanalysis with no new data: 'The data in this paper were taken from Sneddon's (1975) grammar of Tondano' (p. 16); takes Sneddon's 'stress usually falls on the penultimate syllable' as a right-aligned trochee, assumes long vowels and coda consonants are moraic and schwa non-moraic, and derives final stress after penult schwa and long-vowel/antepenult cases from Sneddon's examples (pp. 16-17). 'Sneddon (1975) describes only primary stress and no secondary stress' (p. 16).
sources.note: Only dedicated paper on Tondano stress found; OT reanalysis of Sneddon's data treating CVC and CVV as bimoraic; secondary, no new data. downloaded now (Internet Archive copy).
